hints.title: Strict Inequality Sorting
hints.text: Sort the elements primarily by nums1 while preserving original indices to easily isolate indices with smaller nums1 values.

hints.title: Batching Equal Values
hints.text: Because the inequality nums1[j] < nums1[i] is strict, process all equal nums1 values in a single batch before adding their nums2 values to the pool.

hints.title: Top-K Sum Tracking
hints.text: Maintain the k largest seen nums2 elements in a min-priority queue and keep their running sum.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import heapq

class Solution:
    def findMaxSum(self, nums1: list[int], nums2: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
        n = len(nums1)
        arr = sorted(zip(nums1, nums2, range(n)))
        ans = [0] * n
        min_heap = []
        current_sum = 0
        
        i = 0
        while i < n:
            j = i
            while j < n and arr[j][0] == arr[i][0]:
                j += 1
            for idx in range(i, j):
                ans[arr[idx][2]] = current_sum
            for idx in range(i, j):
                val2 = arr[idx][1]
                current_sum += val2
                heapq.heappush(min_heap, val2)
                if len(min_heap) > k:
                    current_sum -= heapq.heappop(min_heap)
            i = j
            
        return ans
```

variables: n: length of arrays nums1 and nums2
complexity.notes: Sorting takes O(n log n) time and each element is pushed/popped from a priority queue of size at most k.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Examining all pairs takes O(n^2) which times out for n up to 10^5.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting by nums1 converts multi-criteria filtering into linear prefix processing with a priority queue.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handle strict inequality via batching and maintain top-k elements using a bounded min-heap.
